terminology_note: This fixture set and the code/docs/tests it backs deliberately say 'same-slot scoring-outcome change' or 'scoring outcome change', never 'official score review' or 'confirmed reversal'.

The evidence below proves the PUBLISHED OUTCOME changed (GOAL -> BEHIND) at an identical match-clock/player/team/scoreEvent slot. It does not prove WHY -- no explicit review, correction, or umpiring-decision field or marker exists anywhere in the commentaryFeed payload. Asserting 'official review' would be inferring intent the source data does not supply.

This wording was corrected after initial review feedback on the PR that introduced this fixture set; the original wording ('official score-review reversal') overstated what the evidence actually shows.

commentary_CD_M20260142406_full.json.key_finding: At periodNumber=3, periodSeconds=839, this real final array contains ONLY 'BEHIND - Bulldogs (Cody Weightman)'. The earlier 'GOAL - Bulldogs (Cody Weightman)' text (see the live diagnostic evidence below) is NOT present anywhere in this array. This proves the upstream feed itself can replace an entry's text in place between polls -- it does not necessarily retain every historical version forever.

A reduced subset of commentary_CD_M20260142406_full.json (the real final capture) -- every event in this file is copied verbatim from that real response; nothing is fabricated. Demonstrates the real final state: only the BEHIND remains at the period=3/839s slot.

explanation: The user's originally attached JSON ('.response.json') and text report for this issue are both for CD_M20260142409, which shows no same-slot scoring-outcome change in either supplied file.

The SAME text report also summarises several other Round 24 matches captured by the same diagnostic run, and CD_M20260142406's section contains a real, diagnostic-detected 'possible edits/changes' entry pairing a GOAL with a later BEHIND at the identical slot -- see the live-poll-sequence source above.
That pairing is a genuine, real change in published scoring outcome, not a fabricated scenario. It is the real evidence Issue #201 asked to be found in the supplied Round 24 captures.

The diagnostic text report only records structured per-event fields (seq, timestamp, period, player, team, scoreEvent, comment) for score events and quarter markers -- it does not preserve a verbatim full commentaryEvent[] array snapshot of the EARLIER (before-the-change) moment the way a raw Bruno '.response.json' capture does. commentary_CD_M20260142406_score_review_poll1.json therefore remains a reconstruction of that earlier moment, using the real field values from the report.

After initial PR review, the repository owner supplied the real final concluded-match capture directly (commentary_CD_M20260142406_full.json), which replaced what had previously been a second reconstructed 'poll2' fixture. This upgraded the 'after' state of this fixture set from a reconstruction to a genuine raw capture, and revealed that the upstream feed had NOT retained the earlier GOAL text alongside the BEHIND -- only the BEHIND remains. commentary_CD_M20260142406_score_review_poll2.json is a reduced, verbatim subset of that real file.

notes: Persisting poll1 then poll2 through afl_json.match_commentary.persist_commentary_feed must produce TWO distinct match_commentary_events rows for period=3/839s (the GOAL, first observed from poll1; the BEHIND, first observed from poll2), never one row silently overwritten by the other -- even though the real upstream feed's own array (poll2, and commentary_CD_M20260142406_full.json) no longer contains the GOAL text at all.
The BEHIND row must be linked via possible_edit_of_event_id to the GOAL row's internal id, since both share playerId=CD_I1011803 (non-null) and an identical slot key.

Both rows must remain visible, in their original first_observed_at order, from GET /api/v1/matches/{match_id}/commentary -- this is the concrete behavioural difference between AFL-api's own append-only history and the upstream feed's apparent in-place mutability.
